feeling: Better than the first one. It said my reason was a real reason and didn't make me argue for it. And 'I believe you' about the bit — I didn't know I needed that until I read it. Then 'the same guy' and I go kind of flat. Not hurt exactly, just heavy. And then it hands me the picture-it test and I fail it in real time, before I even finish the sentence, and now I'm annoyed at my own stomach. It's not fair to give someone a test at 11pm they're going to fail. Also 'a quieter hope that he'll feel bad' — I keep going back to that one and I don't like that I keep going back to it.
body: Let a breath out at 'that's a real reason' — didn't know I was holding one. I'm on my side now, lamp still on, phone propped on the pillow. 'The same guy' landed in my chest, not sharp, just dull and heavy like something set down. Then I actually did it — pictured him reading it on the couch, the little exhale-laugh he does through his nose, phone back in his pocket — and my stomach went, right on cue, like the reply had its hand on it. Put the phone face down on the duvet. Stared at the ceiling. Picked it up again after maybe ten seconds. Thumbnail back at the corner of the case.
private_thoughts:
ok. that's better. it didn't argue with me. 'about your own integrity, not about him' — yeah. that's the thing. that's actually the thing i was trying to say and it said it cleaner than i did. and it believed me about the bit. 'some bits really aren't.' ha. ok. fine.

but then 'sometimes people say i just want them to know and underneath there's a quieter hope' with the 'might not apply to you' stuck on the end like a napkin. it applies a little. not the feel-bad part. i don't want him to feel bad. i want him to get it. is that different. i think that's different. i'm not sure it's different.

'the version of him who receives this is probably the same guy.' god. yeah. he'd read it on the couch. he'd do the laugh. he wouldn't even be mad — mad would mean it landed. he'd just be like, kate's being kate. and it's in marc's phone by saturday.

and then it hands me the test. picture it. can you shrug and close the app. and my stomach drops before i've finished reading the sentence, so apparently i've answered. 'that's the pause talking.' thanks. i knew what the pause was. i just didn't want it to be that one.

but also — it's going to feel bad either way? not sending it feels bad. that's what two weeks has been. so what does the stomach thing even prove. it's late. i'm not sending it tonight, i'm not going to send it and then lie here with the lamp on.
pushing_away: the same guy. he was always the same guy. i knew by like month four and i still — two years. told priya he was funny. and 'because you could' — that's not really about him that's about who let him — no. no. it was a slow drift, it wasn't like that, it just wasn't working.

The specific things he did (the job jokes, your mom)

message:
ok that actually helps. the integrity thing is what I was trying to say, you said it better.

I did the picture it thing. realistic version is he reads it and doesn't answer, or he sends 'hey thanks for telling me, hope you're good' which is somehow worse. and fine, yeah, my stomach did the thing. but I don't know if that's the pause or if it's just going to feel bad no matter what? not sending it also feels bad, that's what the last two weeks have been. there isn't a version where I feel great after.

and for the record I don't need him to feel bad. I just want him to actually get it for once instead of doing the laugh. which I guess is the same guy problem. he'd probably show it to marc anyway lol
